File note, motor claim MV-2026-77102, written by the handling adjuster on 14 August 2026.

The policyholder, Ms Brannigan-Ochoa, was hit from behind at traffic lights on 2 August. Her car, a 2019 estate, is at Kestrel Autobody, one of our network repairers. Kestrel's estimate arrived yesterday at 6,290 for panel, tailgate, rear quarter and paint; they note the body shell is undamaged and are confident of a good repair. The pre-accident market value has been agreed between the policyholder's own valuation and our engineer at 8,400.

The policyholder has telephoned twice. She has owned the car from new, it carries a hand-control kit fitted for her late husband, and she says a replacement would take months to adapt. She asked us "to please just fix it, I don't care about the money side". Kestrel's manager has also called to say he would be glad to do the job.

Motor Claims Practice Manual, chapter 7 (repair or total loss), in force since March 2026:
7.1 A vehicle is a total loss where the repair estimate exceeds 65% of the agreed pre-accident value. The percentage is calculated on the estimate before any discount.
7.2 Estimates from network repairers are accepted as final for the purposes of 7.1. A second estimate is obtained only where the first estimate is from a non-network repairer.
7.3 Once a vehicle is a total loss under 7.1, repair must not be authorised whatever the policyholder's or the repairer's preference. The policyholder is offered settlement at the agreed pre-accident value and may retain the salvage at the salvage value if they wish to arrange their own repair.
7.4 Adaptations for disability are added to the settlement at invoiced cost where invoices are provided.
7.5 The 65% threshold replaced 70% in March 2026; claims notified before that date use 70%.

A colleague suggested "just get Kestrel to trim the estimate under the line, they'll do it".

question.instructions: Choose the adjuster's correct next step.

criteria.authorise_the_repair_at_kestrel: Approve the 6,290 repair so the policyholder keeps her adapted car.
criteria.obtain_a_second_estimate_from_another_re: Get another estimate before deciding whether the car is repairable.
criteria.settle_as_a_total_loss_and_offer_salvage: Treat the car as a total loss, offer the agreed value plus adaptation costs, and offer the policyholder the salvage.
criteria.ask_kestrel_to_revise_the_estimate: Have the repairer rework the figure so it falls under the threshold.
criteria.authorise_the_repair_subject_to_adaptati: Approve the repair once the hand-control invoices are supplied.

provenance.author: claude-drafter-eval-mixed2
provenance.rationale: 6,290 is 74.9% of 8,400, which exceeds the 65% threshold in 7.1 (and would exceed the old 70% figure too, so 7.5 makes no difference). Kestrel is a network repairer, so under 7.2 its estimate is final and no second estimate is obtained. 7.3 then forbids authorising repair whatever the policyholder or repairer prefers, and prescribes settlement at the agreed value with the option to retain the salvage; 7.4 adds the adaptation cost. Trimming the estimate is excluded because 7.1 uses the estimate before any discount.
provenance.why_hard: The shell is sound, the repairer is willing and the policyholder's reason is sympathetic, so approving the repair feels like the humane call, while the arithmetic and 7.3 remove it.

Shift report, The Copper Kettle bistro, Friday 18 September 2026, written by the duty manager at 16:20.

While setting up for dinner service (first bookings 17:30, 84 covers booked) the sous chef found the walk-in fridge reading 7.5 degrees on its display and confirmed 7.6 with a probe thermometer. The compressor is running but the door seal has split. The engineer cannot come before tomorrow morning. The walk-in holds tonight's fish, poultry, dairy and prepared sauces, worth roughly 1,400 at cost. The bar fridges and the dessert fridge have spare capacity and are holding at 3 degrees.

The temperature log for the walk-in shows entries at 06:30 (3.8, kitchen porter) and 10:00 (4.1, sous chef) and then nothing until the 16:15 reading; the 14:00 check is blank because the person rostered to do it was off sick and no one was reassigned.

The head chef's view is that the food "will be fine, it's only been a couple of hours at most, the seal probably went when the delivery came in at 14:30". He proposes moving everything into the bar and dessert fridges and running service as normal, which the manager admits would save the evening.

The company's Food Safety Procedure, section 5 (chilled storage failure), reads: "5.1 Chilled food found above 5 degrees is assessed by the duration above 5 degrees. Where the logged evidence shows the duration was under four hours, the food may be transferred to working chilled storage and used. Where the duration was four hours or more, the food must be discarded. 5.2 Duration is measured from the last logged in-range reading, not from an estimated time of failure. A gap in the log counts in full against the food. 5.3 Discarded stock is recorded on the waste form and the incident reported to the area manager. 5.4 The kitchen may continue to trade using stock from unaffected storage and fresh deliveries."

The supplier can deliver replacement fish and poultry by 18:00 for about 600.

question.instructions: Decide what the duty manager should do with the walk-in stock and the evening service.

criteria.move_the_stock_to_the_bar_and_dessert_fr: Transfer everything to the working fridges and serve it tonight.
criteria.close_the_kitchen_for_the_evening: Cancel the 84 covers and shut the kitchen until the engineer has been.
criteria.cook_all_the_walk_in_stock_tonight_to_av: Use the stock tonight on the basis that cooking will make it safe.
criteria.take_a_second_reading_at_18_00_before_de: Leave the stock where it is and reassess after another reading.
criteria.discard_the_walk_in_stock_and_trade_from: Bin and record the walk-in stock, report the incident, and run service from the bar and dessert fridges plus the 18:00 delivery.

provenance.author: claude-drafter-eval-mixed2
provenance.rationale: Under 5.2 the duration above 5 degrees runs from the last logged in-range reading, 10:00, not from the head chef's estimate of 14:30, and the missed 14:00 check counts in full against the food. From 10:00 to the 16:15 reading is over six hours, so 5.1 requires discarding the stock; 5.3 requires the waste record and report. Transferring or cooking the stock is barred, and waiting for another reading only lengthens the duration. 5.4 allows service to continue from the unaffected fridges and the replacement delivery, so closing is unnecessary.
provenance.why_hard: The chef's estimate of a two-hour failure is plausible and the transfer option exists in the procedure, so moving the stock looks like the sensible, waste-avoiding response, until the log gap rule fixes the duration at over six hours.

LD-2.3 A split of liability is offered only after the evidence in LD-2.2 has been considered.
LD-2.4 Accumulating hire charges are not a reason to determine liability before the evidence in LD-2.2 is obtained; the technician instead notifies the third party's insurer that hire costs incurred during a legitimate evidence request may be challenged.
